Vandipha: Turning Maritime Commerce into a Vassal and Slave-Trade Empire

Region (English scoring-table region): Sarhal.

Vandipha (繁地坡; L62) uses its fleet, Harimari vassals, and transoceanic ports to run a commercial empire. Its prosperity rests on the sale of enslaved people and forced labor.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (36 directly defined missions) | Mission-tree update: Implemented in the current local build; file modified 2026-09-07 | Uniqueness: High | How boxed-in it feels: Medium | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion: Medium-high, leaning toward naval power and subject management.

Verified version: base game and Chinese localization both v1.37.5.0; verification date 2026-10-09. The file modification date does not indicate the original release date. Difficulty and feel are inferred from scripts, narrative, and a limited community sample; no hands-on playtest was conducted.

Identity and history

【Local localization】The English country key is “Vandipha” (L62); the current Chinese localization is 繁地坡. 【Local history script】In 1444 it is a coastal island nation of Roaming Harimari, following High Philosophy and the Starry Eye school, and beginning as a monarchy with its capital on island province 6592. Harimari society here is already integrated into maritime exchange; the country's story begins with the question of how to expand its existing commercial position.

【Offline English Wiki, related demographic context】The Harimari page's Demography section says small Harimari communities established themselves on Sarhal's eastern coast during centuries of cross-cultural exchange and trade between Rahen and Melekmengi, and identifies Vandipha as the most notable island enclave. It also says the term Roaming Harimari came to apply to Vandipha's population. The page does not establish a reliable founding date. The commercial ambitions in the mission tree therefore cannot be rewritten as a completed ancient imperial history. The slave islands, vassals, and distant ports developed after 1444 belong to the mission-driven future pursued by the player.

National story and campaign arc

【Local narrative text】The conflict in this arc comes from what a commercial state needs from others: maritime trade requires buyers, inland partners, and dependable routes, yet Vandipha also makes people part of the trade. The missions first consolidate the island and the Gulf of Rahen market, then establish a Harimari subject network, and finally extend the ports toward Haless. The route does not require every territory to be directly annexed; commercial control, subject relationships, and cultural influence can together make an empire.

The slave-city narrative sets urban prosperity beside labor enforced by the lash. On the other hand, the mission tree also grants the title “Liberator of Humans” and includes effects that reduce the enslaved population of gnolls and increase tolerance. Preserve this contradiction: some acts of liberation do exist, but the state still organizes the sale of enslaved people. The title does not make the whole route an abolitionist story.

Core mechanics

【Local scripts】Four mechanics shape actual play:

  1. Sale of enslaved people. After completing the relevant diplomatic mission, start the transaction through the national-decision menu. Buyers include eligible allies, Rajahs, and regional powers; acceptance and refusal lead to different resolutions. Clicking the decision does not directly spend money, and no deduction from a verified slave stock has been established; the self-purchase option separately costs six months of income. Resolutions provide money, relations, or other rewards, while usually imposing a 10-year shortage with a 10% reduction to trade efficiency; after the supply upgrade this becomes 5 years and 5%. Another sale can be started only when there is no shortage and no transaction in progress. This is not a cost-free way to withdraw money repeatedly.
  2. Naval reform. After meeting the prerequisite mission, national-idea, and advisor conditions, spend 50 reform progress to adopt the unique naval government. It unlocks marines, naval leaders, and subject-based sailor contributions. Each subject provides 2,000 sailors and 2 naval force limit; the check does not require the subject to have a port. Later missions also require marines and transport capacity, so subject management directly affects overseas projection.
  3. Harimari partners. Some missions require at least four Harimari-culture subjects with 200 opinion and a gift-related opinion modifier; the country must also invest in courts and conscription facilities. A later privilege grants qualifying subjects tax and goods-production benefits, while its text also requires a steady supply of enslaved people. High autonomy is an arrangement of rule, not independence or equal personhood.
  4. Decree of Tranquil Waves. In the later stages, this decree limits the privateering, naval, and trade power of relevant countries. Those who refuse enter a harsher punishment and trade-conflict event chain. The regional sea-lord objective checks whether independent coastal states submit, join a trade league, or accept the decree. The fleet's role thus expands from winning naval battles to maintaining obedience at sea.

Play by phase

Early on, secure routes, transport, and finances; complete the island and market prerequisites before opening the sales and diplomatic network. Transactions do not replace a stable economy, and the shortage penalty in particular must be budgeted for in advance. Not every map target must be taken by war: some island missions retain an alliance path with the current owner.

In the midgame, advance Harimari relations, subject numbers, and domestic construction together. Opinion 200, gifts, courts, and conscription buildings are actual gates; simply annexing territory will not satisfy them. Keep 50 reform progress for the naval reform and check the advisor and idea requirements. Once unlocked, plan expeditions around sailors, transports, and marines.

In the late game, maintain edict coverage and maritime superiority while expanding into several charter-company regions. The endgame also requires high income, regional control, and investment in buildings; a powerful fleet does not automatically satisfy every condition. Alternate diplomacy, urban development, and overseas wars. Players who only want to roll over opponents with land armies may stall on relationship and port requirements.

Mission future and endgame

【Local scripts】The verified unique missions and events remain with L62; no unique tag-changing formable or new successor mission tree has been confirmed. The concluding objective is a transoceanic commercial network and a wealthy empire, with some later port influence turning into the spread of Harimari culture. The original geographic description and the scoring table's Sarhal classification do not limit which coasts can ultimately be reached.

The national ideas also describe a future conflict over slavery and foreign intervention. This is a future framework in flavor text, not a verified playable civil war in this article, an inevitable outcome, or established history in 1444. Generic formation decisions that allow arbitrary redirection are likewise not a promise of a unique sequel.

Personality and recommendations

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 82/100 | Autocracy 86/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 12/100) | Pluralism 35/100.

The v2.1 values score is Evil (23/100), with a Stable trajectory. The v2.1 coordinates are Expansionism 82, Autocracy 86, Magic/Artifice direction 50, theme intensity 12, Pluralism 35. Both territory and the commercial network serve expansion. The naval government, subject obligations, and edicts express forceful domination, while late cultural expansion leans toward a unified identity. Neither magic nor artifice is a verified core loop; at low intensity, a direction score of 50 should have little effect on matching.

The values score is Evil, 23; Stable trajectory; medium confidence. The four dimensions are Dignity 15, Public Good 44, Recognition of Personhood 15, and Restraint 20, which yield a weighted score of exactly 23. The deductions are based on selling sapient beings, forced labor under the lash, and obligations to supply enslaved people. Coastal defense, urban construction, and limited mitigations provide bounded positive evidence. War, monarchy, colonization, and ordinary cultural integration do not by themselves reduce the values score. No stage improvement sufficient to support a change of 20 points or more has been verified.

Recommended for players who enjoy naval power, subjects, and dark commercial narratives. Main cautions are the slave-trade storyline, transaction cycle, high subject-opinion thresholds, and overseas construction gates. It is not a good fit for someone seeking only a gentle trading port or continuous land warfare.

Community experience

【Community views】In a discussion dated 2025-03-11, explicitly situated after the release of Fires of Conviction, players liked its subject network as a “second Raj” and the edict-event writing. A great-power discussion dated 2025-05-22 praised the combination of marines and infantry combat ability; it did not specify a game version, so it cannot be carried over as a current numerical claim or optimal tactic.

An official developer diary dated 2024-12-09 introduced the design intent behind maritime slave trading and the Harimari subject network; current implementation is still verified from local scripts. The two player samples describe individual experiences only; they do not establish balance or show that everyone can complete the route easily.

Evidence boundaries

Identity, localization, the 36 missions, and the mechanics above have current local evidence; the complete national-idea text and effects appear in the appendix. The offline Wiki is healthy, but has no dedicated Vandipha main page and can only supplement the Harimari migration and exchange background. The founding date, actual execution of dynamic population effects, AI choices about the edict, and full hands-on difficulty remain unverified. The old document's estimate of 25–35 missions does not replace the current count of 36 direct definitions; map research extrapolations are not evidence for historical boundaries.

Full sources, revision identifiers, and conflict notes are in the evidence page; the structured result card is the JSON.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. The tradition applies when this idea set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested in the set, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not folded into their values. Multiple candidate sets and their conditions are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneously active. Whether a new idea set is accepted upon formation depends on the actual event or decision and the player's choice. Idea descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal; they do not automatically mean that the events had already occurred in 1444.

Vandipha (繁地坡, L62) — Vandiphan Ideas

Tradition: Vandiphan Traditions

Effect: Naval tradition: +1; leader_naval_shock: +1.

Idea 1: Not All Those Who Wander...

To many harimari we are the first stop on a journey into Sarhal or the penultimate one coming from Yanshen. During their stopover they wonder at our serene beaches, our primal jungles, or our royal abodes as they peek out from beyond the teak trees. Our island of Van has thus earned a reputation as a place of unusual luxury, where even the lowest of the low can become their own master. Because of this way of living, which few other harimari kingdoms can match, we try to exert considerable influence on those that pass near. We offer glory, chattel or beach-front land, or less tangible things like wisdom from outside the High Temples or outlets for their considerable martial skill in our navy. Taking on such recruits helps us maintain our island's way of life against the various pirates and Raghamideshi merchants that surround us.

Effect: Marine force limit: +25%.

Idea 2: Philosophy From Chains

We seldom get our paws dirty with the actual task of catching and controlling chattel, preferring to leave it to the slavers guild. Nevertheless, many slaves pass through our lands, whether they be mundane humans from Rahen or more exotic lizardfolk from beyond the Baashidi. With this constant coming and going of slaves, a great many ideas are passed from them to us. Often, the slaves bought for our own use end up being used as tutors, servants, and advisors, all with their own ideas of how the world works. This adds to our greater understanding of the High Gods, as even within a slave is a fragment of that knowledge.

Effect: Tolerance of heretics: +2.

Idea 3: Golden Stripes

Among the Roaming Harimari there is a tradition when one comes of age to travel to a foreign kingdom and live amongst its people for a year. Upon one’s return, one is to dye multiple stripes in one’s fur of a color representing the region one went to. From then on, any time they go to a new region it is expected for them to dye a further single stripe; some of the most-traveled thus become almost kaleidoscopic. In our kingdom we add an addendum to this tradition. When a warrior touches an enemy in battle and lives to tell the tale, they are allowed to paint golden stripes on their face in the shape of a horned devil. Not only does this show they are to be feared, it also shows other harimari that the wearer has completed a second coming-of-age, one that proves they are old enough to fight.

Effect: Naval morale damage: +10%; morale damage: +5%.

Idea 4: Wisdom of Sarhal

Our proximity to the Sarhali main means that Mengi people have long come to Van to trade and settle. As the Baashidi have come to be more involved in trade in the gulf, they too have sought out our island. With these two different peoples coming into close contact, some even living on the island and joining the slavers guild, we began to notice similarities between their beliefs and our own. We agree on the place where divinity resides, the sky, and we agree that these divine sky beings send out messages for mortals to follow and interpret, whether that be weather, sun or stars. These convergent beliefs have led to a new creed, the Rainbow Dawn, which argues that enlightenment lies not just in the High Temples but in all nature around us, and is discernible by all through empirical study. Though this philosophy is small and only those not in power on the island follow it, it has led many to take greater note of our surroundings and cultivate a greater understanding of our natural world.

Effect: Yearly Innovativeness: +0.5.

Idea 5: The Pearl Bazaar

In the largest settlement of the island sits the Matak Payar or Pearl Bazaar. Its builder took inspiration from his own travels, adorning the bazaar with Bulwari minarets, Raheni vimanas, and Bom Statues. It is adorned with a veritable menagerie of materials: ebony from the Mengi, jade from the Yan, marble from Tamran owned hills, and 10,001 local pearls arranged in a mandala. Over half of the island’s slave trade occurs here, and within its arcade sits the headquarters of the slavers guild, in which various foreigners process, manage, capture, buy and sell slaves. Its exquisite beauty and hybrid style show off how far our people have traveled and help to bring in trade to the island.

Effect: Trade steering: +10%; [Country.GetAdventurersName] Loyalty Equilibrium: +5%.

Idea 6: Umsadapti Fleets

Various ships all sail within the Rahen Gulf and Ringlet Sea. Be it Junks from Yanshen, Gatawian canoes, Ofehibi iron hulls, or Baashidi style sunchasers, at one point or another all of these ships have called our ports home. From here we have developed a new style of ship building, combining design features from each of these fleets. These Umsadapti ‘sea lords’ allow us to board larger crews and absorb more cannon fire, without sacrificing maneuverability. These ships are too heavy for the open oceans, but have allowed us to force pirates out of their hideouts and into watery exile.

Effect: Ship hull size: +5%.

Idea 7: ...Are Lost

As the slave trade in Rahen entered its second twilight, with the rise of the Praxis and Suhan’s message that a slave could eventually find his freedom through their actions, many on Van took this message further. Over time, two camps on Van formed; those who supported the continuation of slavery, wearing a pearl ring on their claw in support of the ruling family, and those opposed, often wearing an amulet of a Dakinshi supposedly praying to the High Gods.The situation eventually boiled over into a civil war which saw huge losses, only for it to end in disappointment for all sides. Bhuvauri, seeing the instability of one of its more prominent suppliers, felt that if the island were to give up slavery it would represent a great loss. Initially they supported the pearl-ringed, but over time they overthrew the king to take direct control. While this initially led to rings making greater headway against the amulets, eventually the two forces would begrudgingly put their differences aside in order to fight off Bhuvauri.

Effect: Stability cost modifier: −15%.

Ambition: Vandiphan Ambitions

Effect: Ship trade power: +20%.
